home.title: Smart decisions for more
home.description: We combine NASA Earth observation data, soil information, and crop characteristics to explore crop rotation strategies tailored to each field.
home.note: Environmental data to help plan the future of agriculture.

rotation.title: How is a crop rotation generated?
rotation.description: To generate recommendations, we analyze climate conditions, soil characteristics, and the requirements of each crop. This information allows us to apply agricultural criteria to filter and select the most suitable candidate crops.

climate.title: Climate conditions
climate.front: We analyze climate patterns in the area.
climate.back: We use NASA Earth observation data, such as temperature and precipitation, to understand climate conditions and assess which crops may adapt to them.

soil.title: Soil characteristics
soil.front: We consider the conditions of the land where crops will be grown.
soil.back: We evaluate available soil information, such as pH and other relevant properties, to identify which crops can grow under those conditions.

crops.title: Crop requirements
crops.front: We compare each crop's needs with the available conditions.
crops.back: We consult crop characteristics, including temperature, water, and soil requirements. Using these criteria, we filter the options and select candidate crops for rotation.

rotation.result: a selection of candidate crops that may respond to the evaluated conditions and serve as a basis for developing a crop rotation proposal.

app.title: How do you use our application?
app.description: Once the factors that influence crop selection have been identified, our application allows farmers to explore crop rotation alternatives. Discover the process, from registration to generating a recommendation.

register.title: Register your farm
register.description: Farmers enter their personal information, email address, and farm location. They also add the crops included in their current rotation, with the option to register several.

conditions.title: Check your area's conditions
conditions.description: The application displays the information registered by the user along with environmental data for the area, such as humidity and precipitation over the last seven days. From this section, users can start calculating crop rotation alternatives.

explore.title: Explore crop rotation alternatives
explore.description: Based on the information provided, AgroGeo generates three crop rotation proposals. Each alternative shows the crops it includes and explains why it may be suitable for the evaluated conditions.

save.title: Select and save your rotation
save.alt: Details of a selected crop rotation
save.description: Farmers can select one of the alternatives to review the rotation details and learn more about its characteristics. They can also save their chosen proposal to access it later.

nasa.title: Connecting agriculture with NASA data
nasa.description: We integrate environmental information from NASA POWER to complement the analysis of field conditions and support the exploration of crop rotation strategies.
nasa.providesDescription: NASA POWER provides weather information and environmental parameters obtained through satellite observations and analysis models. These data help describe the environmental characteristics of a geographic location.
nasa.usageDescription: We retrieve daily information based on the selected coordinates and time period. The data complements AgroGeo's climate analysis to explore crop rotation alternatives.

hero.description: We combine climate information and crop characteristics to understand the conditions of each field and explore crop rotation alternatives.

nasa.title: NASA POWER data
nasa.heading: Understanding the climate to understand the environment.
nasa.paragraph1: NASA POWER is a NASA platform that provides meteorological information and environmental parameters through satellite observations and analysis models.
nasa.paragraph2: At AgroGeo, we use this data to understand the climate conditions of a geographical area and relate them to the requirements of different crops.
nasa.purposeTitle: WHY DO WE USE THIS DATA?
nasa.purposeDescription: It allows us to analyze variables such as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture, which influence crop development and the selection of potential crop rotation strategies.

meanTemp.name: Mean temperature
meanTemp.description: Average air temperature at 2 meters above the surface.

precipitation.name: Corrected precipitation
precipitation.description: Amount of precipitation used to analyze rainfall conditions.

rootMoisture.name: Root zone moisture
rootMoisture.description: Estimated soil moisture in the area where plant roots grow.

crops.title: Crop data
crops.heading: Every crop has its own requirements.
crops.paragraph1: To complement climate information, we use a CSV file based on FAO ECOCROP data, which brings together the characteristics and environmental requirements of different plant species.
crops.paragraph2: We process this information to identify the conditions each crop needs, including its temperature ranges, precipitation requirements, and soil preferences.
crops.purposeTitle: WHAT DO WE USE THIS INFORMATION FOR?
crops.purposeDescription: It allows us to compare the requirements of each species with the environmental conditions of an area, identifying which crops may be better adapted to the environment.

identification.name: Identification
identification.description: Scientific name and botanical family of the crop.

characteristics.name: Characteristics
characteristics.description: Growth habit, life form, and category.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Optimal temperature ranges and tolerance limits.

precipitation.name: Precipitation
precipitation.description: Rainfall requirements and ranges the crop can tolerate.

soil.name: Soil
soil.description: Soil pH, texture, and depth preferences.

cycle.name: Crop cycle
cycle.description: Minimum and maximum duration of the growing cycle.

gaez.title: FAO GAEZ v4 data
gaez.heading: Understanding what each crop demands from the farm.
gaez.paragraph1: FAO GAEZ (Global Agro-Ecological Zones) is a platform from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations that estimates the attainable yield of different crops according to climate, soil, terrain, and the level of agricultural management.
gaez.paragraph2: At AgroGeo, we compare each crop's attainable yield under high-input farming, which includes mechanization and fertilization, with its yield under low-input farming, based on manual labour and no fertilizer. The difference between both estimates helps us determine how much a crop depends on machinery and inputs.
gaez.purposeTitle: WHY DO WE USE THIS DATA?
gaez.purposeDescription: It allows us to classify each crop's machinery dependence as low, medium, or high. This information feeds the equipment priority and helps rank crop rotation alternatives according to the machinery available to the farmer.

highInput.name: High-input attainable yield
highInput.description: Rain-fed attainable yield (kg/ha) under full mechanization, improved seeds, and fertilizer, based on the 1981–2010 climate.

lowInput.name: Low-input attainable yield
lowInput.description: Rain-fed attainable yield (kg/ha) under manual labour and no fertilizer, using the same climate conditions.

gaez.methodTitle: HOW DO WE OBTAIN THIS DATA?

methodSteps.step1: We query FAO GAEZ's public ImageServer to obtain both yield rasters for each crop available in our catalog.
methodSteps.step2: We sample the data at ten agricultural zones in Colombia: Tunja, Bogotá Savannah, Pasto, Rionegro, Ibagué, Montería, Villavicencio, Piedecuesta, Valledupar, and Palmira.
methodSteps.step3: At each location, we calculate the ratio between high-input and low-input yield. When low-input yield is zero, we apply a cap of 20 to avoid division by zero.
methodSteps.step4: We calculate the median of the resulting ratios and classify crops into three machinery-dependence levels: low, medium, or high.

gaez.coverage: Coverage: 22 of the 41 crops in the catalog.
gaez.limitationDescription: The estimate is based on historical climate conditions from 1981–2010. It helps approximate machinery and input dependence, but it does not represent an inventory of the equipment owned by each farmer.

nass.title: USDA NASS QuickStats data
nass.heading: Adding an economic reference to every crop.
nass.paragraph1: USDA NASS (National Agricultural Statistics Service) is the agency of the United States Department of Agriculture responsible for publishing official agricultural statistics. Through its QuickStats database, it provides information on the prices farmers receive for different agricultural products.
nass.paragraph2: At AgroGeo, we use these prices as an international reference to compare the relative market value of crops that may be included in a rotation, since there is no equivalent open agricultural price API for Colombia.
nass.purposeTitle: WHY DO WE USE THIS DATA?
nass.purposeDescription: It allows us to assign each crop a low, medium, or high reference price level. This classification feeds the economic priority when ranking crop rotation alternatives.

priceReceived.name: Price received by farmers
priceReceived.description: Average annual price received by farmers nationwide in the United States, converted to US dollars per kilogram (USD/kg).

nass.methodTitle: HOW DO WE OBTAIN THIS DATA?

methodSteps.step1: We query the QuickStats API to obtain the annual price received by farmers for each crop at the national level in the United States.
methodSteps.step2: When several price series exist for the same crop, we select the most representative one, such as grain corn or fresh-market tomatoes.
methodSteps.step3: We convert the original units, such as dollars per pound, hundredweight, ton, or bushel, into US dollars per kilogram (USD/kg), using the official weight for each grain.
methodSteps.step4: We calculate the average of the last five years available in our dataset (2021–2025) and classify crops into three price levels: low, medium, or high.

nass.coverage: Coverage: 26 crops, with data from 2021 to 2025.
nass.limitationDescription: These prices correspond to the United States market and are expressed in USD/kg. They are not Colombian prices and do not include production costs. Therefore, AgroGeo uses them only as a comparative reference and acknowledges this difference as a data limitation.

intro.title: Meet the team behind
intro.paragraph1: We chose this challenge with the goal of developing a tool that can support farmers in exploring crop alternatives and recommendations in response to changing climate conditions.
intro.paragraph2: We know that making agricultural decisions means thinking not only about current conditions but also about what may happen in the future. That is why we wanted to make use of technology and environmental data to offer a new perspective on crop possibilities and rotation strategies.
intro.paragraph3: AgroGeo represents our effort to transform information into opportunities that contribute to a more prepared, sustainable, and resilient agriculture.
